findings.title: Recipient's effective slippage tolerance is amplified by 1/(1-f) under non-zero aggregate buffer, breaching the M-02 bounded-leak premise
findings.description: story-042 derives the swap's minOut from the pre-buffer aggregate totalShares (line 434-435), then distributes the proceeds by sending the buffered slice (totalSetAside) to clients[] and only the remainder (toRecipient = underlyingReceived - totalSetAside) to recipient. Define f = totalBufferShares / totalShares (the aggregate buffer fraction). The swap's absolute slippage allowance is unchanged, but the recipient's principal share is reduced by (1-f). Combined with the proportional distribution at line 513, the recipient's per-skim leak as a fraction of recipient yield scales as slippageBps / (1-f): 2x at f=0.5, 10x at f=0.9, 100x at f=0.99. The accepted M-02 bound holds only at f=0 (the deployed default).
findings.economicImpact: Recipient (typically a yield accumulator such as SYA) sees the same absolute slippage Δ amortized over a smaller principal. Per-skim leak relative to recipient take = slippageToleranceBps / (1 - totalBufferFraction).
findings.recommendation: Three layered mitigations: (a) cap slippageToleranceBps to a low ceiling (per L-01); (b) introduce an aggregate buffer cap (see DEDUP-002) so totalBufferFraction is bounded by design; (c) derive minOut against the recipient's share — minOut_recipient = (totalShares - totalBufferShares) * convertToAssets * (MAX_BPS - slippageBps) / MAX_BPS — and revert if toRecipient < minOut_recipient. Per memory feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md, prefer revert over silent clamp.

findings.title: No aggregate cap on per-client buffer percentages allows total set-aside to reach 100% of underlyingReceived, reducing recipient take to zero with no revert
findings.description: setSetAsideBuffer enforces bufferPercent <= 100 per client (line 255). The sum of setAsideBufferSize[client] across the authorized-client set is not capped. With multiple clients at high buffer percentages, totalBufferShares can approach totalShares, in which case toRecipient (line 518) collapses to zero and the entire swap output is redirected to clients[]. The skim completes successfully with no revert, but the withdrawer's recipient parameter is effectively a no-op.
findings.economicImpact: Recipient and any downstream integrator pricing in expected yield from skimSurplus sees zero proceeds despite the swap consuming all surplus value and incurring slippage. Underlying funds are not lost (they remain protocol-owned via the buffered clients) but the keeper/withdrawer/SYA expecting positive flow gets none.
findings.parametricBound: toRecipient ≈ underlyingReceived * (1 - sum(principal[i] * setAsideBufferSize[i]) / (totalDeposited * 100)). At sum-weighted buffer == 100%, toRecipient == 0.
findings.recommendation: Track an aggregate buffer-weight metric on setSetAsideBuffer calls and enforce a configurable ceiling (e.g. aggregateBufferCapBps), OR add a require in _distributeBuffer that toRecipient > 0 (or >= someMin) when totalBufferShares > 0 so an all-clients-at-100 misconfiguration reverts loudly. Per memory feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md, prefer revert-on-malformed-config over silent clamp.

findings.title: setAsideBufferSize persists after a client is deauthorized and silently resurrects on re-auth
findings.description: setSetAsideBuffer (AYieldStrategy.sol#L253-L259) writes setAsideBufferSize[client] = bufferPercent unconditionally — no _authorizedClients.contains(client) check. Symmetrically, setClient(client, false) (L183-L193) removes the address from _authorizedClients but does not zero setAsideBufferSize[client]. The child's _accrueSurplusShares (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol#L487) reads setAsideBufferSize[client] from parent storage during the next skim. If the owner re-authorizes the same address via setClient(client, true), the stale buffer percentage takes effect on the next skim — no re-write required — silently diverting surplus.
findings.impact: Operational footgun. Owner-facing only (centralization-bounded per C-01). No external attacker leverage because every client is protocol-owned (per AYieldStrategy.sol#L246 AUDITOR NOTE). A deployment that toggles client authorization (e.g. rotating an integration's contract address, or temporarily deauthorizing during an incident) silently restores the prior buffer attribution on re-auth, leading to misallocated yield in the next skim. Blast radius is captured by DEDUP-001/DEDUP-002.
findings.exploitSketch: 1) setSetAsideBuffer(clientA, 50). 2) setClient(clientA, false) to migrate. 3) Months later, setClient(clientA, true) to roll back. 4) Without any setSetAsideBuffer call, the next skim sees setAsideBufferSize[clientA] = 50 (the never-zeroed legacy value) and diverts that fraction.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) in setClient(client, false), explicitly zero setAsideBufferSize[client] and emit SetAsideBufferSet(client, oldPercent, 0); or (b) require _authorizedClients.contains(client) in setSetAsideBuffer (rejecting both stale writes and writes to never-authorized addresses); or (c) document the resurrection-on-reauth semantics in the NatSpec. Option (a) gives the cleanest invariant: setAsideBufferSize[client] != 0 ⇒ _authorizedClients.contains(client).

findings.title: SurplusSkimmed event under-represents the buffered-path beneficiaries — no event records per-client buffer redirection
findings.description: On the buffered path, _distributeBuffer (L511-L519) performs underlyingToken.safeTransfer(clients[i], buf) for every surplus-bearing client whose setAsideBufferSize[client] > 0. The only event emitted is SurplusSkimmed(token, client, msg.sender, surplus, recipient) in _accrueSurplusShares (L484), which (a) reports the SNAPSHOT surplus in vault-asset terms (pre-redeem/pre-swap), not the actual underlying received per client; (b) names recipient as the receiver even when most of the proceeds for that client actually go to clients[i]. No event marks the buffer-redirected transfer. Downstream indexers reconstructing fund flow from events will mis-attribute receipts: every wei landing in any clients[i] via the buffered path is invisible to event consumers.
findings.impact: Spec/integration-level only. No tokens lost — all funds reach protocol-owned addresses. Any integrator building reconciliation off SurplusSkimmed (e.g. SYA, or a future analytics consumer) and reading recipient as the destination will silently mis-route accounting under the buffered path. The submodule's own CLAUDE.md note ('skimSurplus return value vs SurplusSkimmed events') only documents the SUM-vs-RETURN-VALUE drift, not the RECIPIENT mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) emit a new SurplusBuffered(token, client, amount) event in _distributeBuffer when buf > 0, and a SurplusForwarded(token, recipient, amount) for the remainder; or (b) extend SurplusSkimmed with a bufferAmount field and emit it in _distributeBuffer rather than _accrueSurplusShares; or (c) document the event semantics under the buffered path in IYieldStrategy.sol NatSpec.

findings.title: skimSurplus return value semantics are path-dependent — fast path returns swap-output, buffered path returns recipient-receipt; CLAUDE.md and NatSpec leave room for integrator confusion
findings.description: FAST PATH (totalBufferShares == 0, L443-L446) returns underlyingReceived = gross swap output = amount to recipient (the two coincide). BUFFERED PATH (L450) returns _distributeBuffer's result, which is toRecipient = underlyingReceived - totalSetAside (the NET amount to recipient). The two paths return semantically-equivalent values ('what arrived at recipient'), but a reviewer reading only the FAST PATH return would conclude the function returns swap output. If a future refactor adds a buffer or tax on the fast path, the return value would silently change semantics. The contract is correct today, but the return-value definition is path-dependent in a non-obvious way. Per econ-scanner C5 verdict, integrators applying a minRewardTokenSupplied floor against the return value ARE protected by construction.
findings.impact: Documentation/integration concern. SYA bubbles underlyingReceived into a 'yield collected' figure; under the buffered path, this number under-counts the protocol's actual realized yield (because the buffer slices are real protocol revenue, routed to a different protocol-owned address). A caller wiring a slippage floor against the return is strictly more conservative under the buffered path — safe, but counter-intuitive.
findings.recommendation: (a) Make the NatSpec on AYieldStrategy.sol#L352-L357 explicit: 'In the buffered path this is REDUCED by the sum of all per-client buffer transfers; use SurplusSkimmed events plus the per-client safeTransfer trace to recover the gross swap output.' (b) Optionally introduce two return values (uint256 toRecipient, uint256 totalSwapped) in a future minor version. (c) Add a unit test that asserts return-value semantics on both paths.

findings.title: setRoute accepts tokenIn == tokenOut and paths with internal zero-gap segments — relies entirely on off-chain verification
findings.description: CurveAMMAdapter.setRoute validates only (a) tokenIn != 0, (b) tokenOut != 0, (c) path[0] == tokenIn, and (d) the LAST non-zero entry in path equals tokenOut. It does NOT check: (i) tokenIn != tokenOut; (ii) that path is contiguously non-zero (e.g. [tokenIn, 0, pool, 0, tokenOut, 0, ...] with internal zero gap passes); (iii) that swapParams matrix or pools array are consistent with the path topology. SA-005 flagged the uninitialized address lastToken at L74 — functionally safe today because path[0]!=0 guarantees lastToken is at least tokenIn, but the broader validation gap is real. Verification is fully delegated to off-chain procedures (per submodule CLAUDE.md AMM Route Configuration section).
findings.impact: Configuration integrity only. Owner-only setter — same trust boundary as the rest of the centralization bundle (C-01). Realistic risk: a typo in deployment scripts produces a route with internal zero gap that passes setRoute, leading to self-DoS at first swap. Tokens cannot be stolen because (a) Curve Router NG enforces minAmountOut, (b) strategy still revert-protects with NAV-anchored minOut. Most plausible bad outcome: strategy brick on deposit/withdraw/skimSurplus until corrected setRoute.
findings.recommendation: Defense-in-depth additions to setRoute: (a) require(tokenIn != tokenOut, 'identity-route'); (b) walk the path validating (token, pool, token, pool, ..., token, 0*) interleave invariant; (c) at minimum reject paths that contain a zero between two non-zero slots.

findings.title: Every swap's minOut is derived from vault.convertToShares / vault.convertToAssets (NAV spot) rather than the AMM clearing price — sandwich-exploitable on routes where NAV diverges from AMM
findings.description: Every swap's minOut is derived from vault.convertToShares/convertToAssets (the external ERC4626 vault's REPORTED share price) scaled by slippageToleranceBps. Since the AMM swap executes against an AMM pool (e.g. Curve), this anchor only protects against the vault's reported price diverging from the AMM clearing price by more than slippageToleranceBps. Scenarios where the ERC4626 vault's share price diverges from AMM (AMM depeg of vault token, withdrawal queue / cooldown distortions like sUSDe) let a flash-trader execute the swap at the unfavourable end of the tolerance band.
findings.impact: Bounded leak of up to slippageBps * tradeSize per swap; economically marginal on the deep sUSDe/USDe pair at normal trade-size-to-depth, growing with looser tolerance, thinner pools, depeg windows, or large swaps. Bounded because sUSDe NAV is not atomically manipulable.
findings.recommendation: Per M-02 acceptance memo (project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md), the residual is accepted by design with the parametric envelope. Compensating control to carry upstream: enforce a sane non-zero floor and a hard ceiling on slippageToleranceBps (per L-01).

findings.title: Sum-of-per-client-floor totalShares produces marginally smaller minOut, weakening slippage protection by clients.length wei
findings.description: totalShares is the SUM of per-client vault.convertToShares(surplus_i) (each independently floored). Sum-of-floors <= floor-of-sum, so totalShares <= vault.convertToShares(aggregateSurplus) is a tautology, making the aggregate-surplus require at L429 effectively defense-in-depth. The minOut computed on this under-counted totalShares is marginally SMALLER than the protocol's fair-share would imply — slightly weakening slippage protection. The drift is bounded by clients.length wei in shares (one wei rounding per client).
findings.impact: Dust-scale weakening of minOut. Bounded by clients.length wei in shares. Per code-scanner verifiedConcerns, the rounding direction (favoring recipient) is intentional and documented.
findings.recommendation: None. The author comment explicitly calls the protocol-favoring rounding intentional. The minOut weakening is dust-scale unless clients.length is large AND the vault's convertToShares has wide rounding error.
